clue.text: Lack of appeal of wild guess, holding nothing back

indicators.note: holding means the scrambled letters hold the other piece inside them
wild suggests something out of control, so the letters of guess are thrown into a new order
back tells us to read the word for nothing in the opposite direction

parts.note: nil means nothing, a score of zero

explanation.surface: Someone's careless guess is criticised as unattractive because it holds nothing back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' looks like it describes the guess, but it scrambles the letters; 'back' turns the zero word round so the shuffle can hold it.
explanation.definitionFit: Ugliness is the quality of being unattractive, a straightforward synonym for lack of appeal.

clue.text: The advantageous aspect attached to this type of clue is seen at sixes and sevens

parts.note: the upside is the good side of a situation
this clue is a down clue in the grid

explanation.surface: The good side of things gets attached to this clue amid utter confusion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'this type of clue' points to the clue's own place in the grid: it is a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Upside down means in complete disorder, the same as the British idiom at sixes and sevens.

clue.text: Couch — a whopper

definitions.meaning: to couch is to recline, as an animal lying in its lair
a whopper is a big untruth

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to recline as couch does, and the noun means an untruth, a whopper.

clue.text: Frank, twenty-one, takes note

definitions.meaning: in pontoon or blackjack, a hand totalling twenty-one with two cards is called this
in music a note that is neither sharp nor flat is called this

explanation.surface: A man called Frank, aged twenty-one, writes something down.
explanation.walkthrough: Three definitions: candid, a perfect pontoon hand, and a musical note neither sharp nor flat; 'takes' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Natural means unaffected and candid, a pontoon hand of twenty-one, and an unaltered musical note.

clue.text: Jacket fitted to a T spirited film star

parts.note: a spencer is a short close-fitting jacket
racy means lively and spirited

explanation.surface: A jacket tailored perfectly to a lively actor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fitted to a T' looks like the idiom for perfectly, but it puts SPENCER beside the letter T.
explanation.definitionFit: Spencer Tracy was a celebrated Hollywood actor, a film star of the 1930s to 1960s.

clue.text: Learn from teacher

definitions.meaning: to ... a skill is to learn it thoroughly
a schoolmaster, especially in old British usage, is a male teacher

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for acquiring a skill fully and a noun for a schoolteacher.

clue.text: A maiden, girl found in the country

parts.note: M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over
Erica is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A young woman and a girl are found living abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maiden' looks like a girl, but it is cricket's maiden over, M.
explanation.definitionFit: America is commonly used for the country the United States.

clue.text: Runny adhesive used by a builder — I've forgotten its name

parts.note: something thin is watery, runny
gum is a glue
Bob the Builder is a children's television character

explanation.surface: A builder uses some watery glue for which no one remembers the name.
explanation.walkthrough: BOB comes from Bob the Builder, a British children's TV cartoon character.
explanation.definitionFit: A thingumabob is a placeholder word used when you cannot recall what something is called.

clue.text: A lot of water transport

definitions.meaning: a ... of things is a large number of them
a flat floating platform of logs used to travel on water

explanation.definitionFit: The word means a large collection, as in a raft of measures, and a flat floating craft.

clue.text: Climber takes dessert with vegetable accompaniment

parts.note: a sweet is the British word for a pudding or dessert
peas are a common vegetable side served with a main course

explanation.surface: A mountaineer enjoys a pudding along with some vegetables on the side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Climber' suggests a mountaineer, but it is a climbing garden plant.
explanation.definitionFit: The sweet pea is a climbing plant grown for its scented flowers, so it is a botanical climber.

clue.text: Umpire has 2 in reserve

indicators.note: in means the cross-referenced word goes inside the official

parts.note: ref is the short form of referee, an umpire
2 refers to the answer to 2 down, the word meaning couch or a whopper

explanation.surface: An umpire is held back as a substitute, kept in reserve.
explanation.walkthrough: The '2' is a cross-reference: put the answer to 2 down inside REF.
explanation.definitionFit: Relief troops or a relief driver are a reserve brought in to take over, so the noun fits.

clue.text: Ladies' men freak out when dogs are around

indicators.note: are around means the dogs surround the other piece

parts.note: poodles are a breed of dog

indicators.note: out suggests disorder, so the letters of freak are rearranged

explanation.surface: Womanisers panic when dogs come near.
explanation.walkthrough: 'freak out' reads as panic, but 'out' only rearranges the letters of freak; poodle-faker is dated British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: A poodle-faker is dated British slang for a man who courts women's company, a ladies' man.

clue.text: Bill's gone ahead with navigational calculation

indicators.note: ahead tells us the word for gone is placed in front of the word for bill

parts.note: gone can mean dead, departed
a reckoning is a bill or account to be settled

explanation.surface: Someone's bill has gone through ahead of a navigator's calculation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a man's name, but it is an account to pay.
explanation.definitionFit: Dead reckoning is the method of estimating a ship's position from its speed, course and time elapsed.

clue.text: I'd given star unusual publicity

indicators.note: unusual means the letters appear in an odd order

explanation.surface: Someone is praised for providing a star with exceptional promotion.
explanation.definitionFit: Advertising is the business of publicising products, a form of publicity.

clue.text: Devise the case for Jarndyce, appearing regularly regardless

indicators.note: the case for means the word for devise forms a container round the other letters

parts.note: to devise is to invent

indicators.note: appearing regularly means alternate letters of the name are taken

explanation.surface: A lawyer devises the argument in the Dickens case Jarndyce, which keeps recurring.
explanation.walkthrough: Jarndyce v Jarndyce is the endless lawsuit in Dickens's Bleak House; 'case' is a container, not a lawsuit.
explanation.definitionFit: In any event is an idiom meaning whatever happens, so regardless.

clue.text: Wicked person was about

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the word for was is read from its end

parts.note: lived can stand for was, as in existed

explanation.surface: A villain was hanging around somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like a link meaning approximately but it signals the turnaround of LIVED.
explanation.definitionFit: A devil is a cruel or wicked person, an extension of the evil spirit sense.

clue.text: With some training, lands more fish

indicators.note: training reshapes something, so these letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: An angler who practises a bit catches more fish.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a fisherman improving, but 'With some training' rearranges LANDS MORE.
explanation.definitionFit: The red salmon, also called sockeye, is a Pacific species of salmon, a kind of fish.

clue.text: Staff available prove practicable and appropriate to church

parts.note: a plan that works proves practicable
for can mean suitable or appropriate to, as in a job for him
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Available employees show the scheme works and is suited to the church.
explanation.definitionFit: A workforce is the body of employees available to an organisation, its staff.

clue.text: A lot of money paid out to get air

parts.note: one pays out for something one wants to get
an air is a melody or tune

explanation.surface: A fortune is spent just to get some fresh air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'air' looks like the atmosphere but it is a melody.
explanation.definitionFit: A fortune is a large sum of money, as in costing a fortune.

clue.text: Building providing vehicle with home

parts.note: a cab is a taxi, a vehicle
in means at home

explanation.surface: A building comes with a car and a house included.
explanation.definitionFit: A cabin is a small simple building, typically a hut made of wood.

clue.text: Bit of oil in motor encompassing velocity zero

indicators.note: encompassing means the car surrounds the other letters

parts.note: a motor is a car
mph, miles per hour, is a measure of velocity
O looks like zero

explanation.surface: A drop of oil in an engine runs at no speed.
explanation.definitionFit: Camphor is a strong-smelling compound from the camphor tree, found in its essential oil.

clue.text: Climber entangled with aerial that can't be saved

indicators.note: entangled suggests twisting and mixing, so the letters of both words are mixed up

explanation.surface: A climber caught up in a television aerial is beyond rescue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entangled' mixes the letters of CLIMBER and AERIAL together; 'with' only joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: Irreclaimable describes something lost beyond recovery or rescue, so it means unsavable.

clue.text: Gem given by old friend

parts.note: a pal is a friend

explanation.surface: A jewel given by an old friend.
explanation.definitionFit: Opal is a gemstone known for its shifting play of colour.

clue.text: Puritanical American bishop

parts.note: prim means prudish and strait-laced

explanation.surface: An American bishop is described as puritanical.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Scottish Episcopal Church the presiding bishop is called the Primus.
explanation.definitionFit: Primus is the title of the presiding bishop of the Scottish Episcopal Church.

clue.text: Fish moves south along the coast

indicators.note: moves means one letter is shifted to a new place along the word

parts.note: the seashore is the coast

explanation.surface: A fish is heading south, following the shoreline.
explanation.walkthrough: Shifting one S along SEASHORE three places gives the answer; 'along' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: The sea horse is a small fish with a horse-like head that swims upright.

clue.text: Regret as currency rises finally missing out

indicators.note: rises in a down clue means the letters are read upwards, back to front
finally missing out means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: the euro is a European currency

explanation.surface: Someone regrets that the currency is rising, so in the end they miss out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally missing out' cuts EURO to EUR, and 'rises' turns it upwards in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To rue something is to regret it bitterly.

clue.text: Boy carrying bomb around fell behind

indicators.note: carrying means the boy holds the other piece inside him

parts.note: a lad is a boy

indicators.note: around means the word for bomb is turned back to front

parts.note: egg is old slang for a bomb, especially an aerial one

explanation.surface: A boy carrying a bomb dropped behind the others.
explanation.walkthrough: Egg as slang for a bomb is RAF wartime usage; 'around' turns it, and 'carrying' sets it inside the boy.
explanation.definitionFit: To lag is to fall behind, so lagged is the past tense matching fell behind.

clue.text: Hungry retinues need cooking

indicators.note: cooking prepares raw ingredients, so the letters of retinues are reworked

explanation.surface: A royal entourage is starving and needs a meal prepared.
explanation.definitionFit: Esurient is a formal or humorous word for greedy or hungry, from Latin esurire.
